c.tagline: First Ottoman capital, cradled by Mount Uludağ and steaming with silk and thermal springs.

taxi.fareNote: Yellow taxis are metered; the BiTaksi app and Uber both dispatch licensed metered taxis rather than private cars.

emergency.note: 112 is Türkiye's unified emergency number connecting to ambulance, fire and police.

avoid.reason: Watch pockets in the crowded Grand Bazaar and Kapalicarsi lanes, and insist taxis run the meter.

hood_desc: Bursa's historic core around Ulu Cami (the Grand Mosque), the covered bazaar and the Koza Han silk khan, and Heykel square — the walkable heart where first-timers should base themselves for sights, shopping and İskender kebab.
The hillside thermal-spa quarter west of center, famous since Roman and Ottoman times for its hot springs; lined with spa hotels and quiet leafy streets, ideal for a relaxed soak-and-stay.
Bursa's modern western district of wide avenues, university campuses, shopping malls and contemporary restaurants and bars — the newer city center where dining and nightlife concentrate.
The eastern district holding the Green Mosque and Green Tomb (Yeşil Cami and Yeşil Türbe) and the Emir Sultan complex; a traditional, sight-rich quarter of early-Ottoman monuments.
A 700-year-old UNESCO-listed Ottoman village on the lower slopes of Mount Uludağ, about 10 km east, with cobbled lanes and painted timber houses; a tranquil escape known for its village breakfasts.
lodging: Almira Hotel Thermal Spa & Convention Center

water.note: Locals often drink the mountain-fed tap water, but most visitors stick to bottled.

transit.hours: Bursaray and city buses run roughly 6:00 AM to midnight; there is no dedicated night service, so taxis or ride apps cover late hours.
transit.note: Bursa's backbone is the Bursaray light-metro line crossing the city east-west, complemented by tram lines and the extensive BURULAŞ city bus network.
transit.pay: Travel is paid with the rechargeable BuKart smart card tapped on entry; single fares are low and transfers between metro, tram and bus are discounted. Contactless bank cards work on many lines.

bus: Intercity coaches from Bursa Terminal (Otogar) to Istanbul, Ankara and İzmir
ferry: BUDO / İDO fast ferries across the Sea of Marmara between Mudanya/Güzelyalı and Istanbul
train: Bursaray light rail (no mainline intercity rail station in the city)

transit.m: Municipal bus toward Yenişehir/city (limited daytime service, ~75 min)
Note: many travelers instead fly into Istanbul and take the BUDO/İDO fast ferry across the Sea of Marmara to Mudanya, then a short bus into Bursa.

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% for good service in restaurants is appreciated but not expected.
